claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is homogeneous, as-cast, and equiatomic.
A combinatorial powder-metallurgy approach can be used to vary individual element percentages in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changing individual element percentages in HfNbTaTiZr will produce systematic changes in mechanical properties.
The mechanical-property changes will occur particularly through changes in solid-solution strengthening and phase stability.
High-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering can be used to process and consolidate the alloy powders.
Room-temperature compression testing at a controlled strain rate is applicable to powder-metallurgy HEA specimens.
Changing element percentages alters the local bonding environment.
Changing element percentages causes variations in lattice distortion.
Changing element percentages causes variations in phase fractions.
Changing element percentages causes variations in grain-boundary characteristics.
Composition modification changes the degree of solid-solution strengthening.
Composition modification may promote or hinder secondary-phase formation.
Changes in solid-solution strengthening and secondary phases alter dislocation motion.
Changes in solid-solution strengthening and secondary phases alter grain-refinement processes.
Altered dislocation motion and grain refinement affect mechanical strength and ductility.
Modest composition changes are expected to increase strength through improved solid-solution effects.
Beyond a composition threshold, phase segregation or excessive lattice distortion may reduce ductility.
The effects are expected to be significant only over a limited range of composition changes.
Large departures from equiatomic composition may produce additional phases or phase instabilities.

contradictions.description: The initial state is specified as an as-cast alloy, whereas the baseline and modified samples are specified as powder-metallurgy materials. This makes it unclear whether the operative baseline is as-cast or ball-milled and SPS-consolidated.
